fullPassage: Suppose that you find information about something on the internet. Among the many search results, which link will you click? Probably, the most attractive and eye-catching one. However, the information you have just found may not be valid even though it looks like it is. For example, assume that you have typed in "piano tuner" in the search engine. As a search result, you see a video of an adorable cat playing the piano. Would you click on it? You would, along with many others, even though it has nothing to do with piano tuning. The search engine then learns that the video is relevant to piano tuning and that it is okay to show a cat playing the piano when people are searching for piano tuners. This isn't just true for search engines, but also on social media platforms, which learn based on what you and others have clicked on before, not based on the accuracy of the information. In other words, the search engine learns that the link you previously clicked on is relevant to your search question, even though it is not. When this irrelevant information, however, is clicked frequently enough, it can appear to be relevant and then mislead internet users.

det.tip: have nothing to do with = ~과 관련 없다 (do = 관련). What can ~ do = 무엇을 할 수 있을까 (do = 하다)

questions.stem:
다음 영영 풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"to cause someone to believe something that is not true; to lead someone in the wrong direction"

det.korean: 사실이 아닌 것을 믿게 하다; 잘못된 방향으로 이끌다 = mislead(오도하다)
det.analysis:
✅ ④ mislead: 사실이 아닌 것을 믿게 하여 잘못된 방향으로 이끄는 것
❌ ① inform(알리다): 정보를 제공하는 것. 오도와 반대
❌ ② assume(가정하다): 추측하는 것. 이끄는 행위 아님
❌ ③ attract(끌다): 주의를 끄는 것. 잘못된 방향과 무관
det.tip: mislead = mis(잘못) + lead(이끌다). 동의어: deceive(속이다), delude(기만하다)

questions.passage: This isn't just true for search engines, but also on social media platforms. They learn not based on the __________ (accurate) of the information, but on how often links are clicked.
questions.stem: 다음 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (1단어) (영어로) (   ) 쓰시오.

det.analysis: the + __________ + of: 관사와 전치사 사이에는 명사가 필요. accurate(형용사) → accuracy(명사)
det.tip: accurate(형용사: 정확한) → accuracy(명사: 정확성). the + 명사 + of 구조

questions.passage: When this irrelevant information is clicked frequently enough, it can appear to be __________ (relevance) and then mislead internet users. The search engine learns that the link you previously clicked on is connected to your search question.
questions.stem: 다음 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (1단어) (영어로) (   ) 쓰시오.

det.analysis: appear to be + __________: be동사 뒤에 형용사 보어 필요. relevance(명사) → relevant(형용사)
det.tip: relevance(명사: 관련성) → relevant(형용사: 관련 있는). appear to be + 형용사

questions.passage: Suppose that you find information about something on the internet. Among the many search results, which link will you click? Probably, the most attractive and eye-catching one. However, the information you have just found may not be valid even though ____. For example, assume that you have typed in "piano tuner" in the search engine. As a search result, you see a video of an adorable cat playing the piano. Would you click on it? You would, along with many others, even though it has nothing to do with piano tuning. The search engine then learns that the video is relevant to piano tuning and that it is okay to show a cat playing the piano when people are searching for piano tuners. This isn't just true for search engines, but also on social media platforms, which learn based on what you and others have clicked on before, not based on the accuracy of the information. In other words, the search engine learns that the link you previously clicked on is relevant to your search question, even though it is not. When this irrelevant information, however, is clicked frequently enough, it can appear to be relevant and then mislead internet users.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: no one has clicked on it

det.korean: 비록 그래 보이더라도(it looks like it is) 유효하지 않을 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① it looks like it is: 원문 일치. '유효해 보이더라도 유효하지 않을 수 있다'는 역접
❌ ④ it is completely false: 아예 거짓이라면 may not be가 아니라 is not이 자연스러움
❌ ② no one has clicked on it: 클릭 여부와 유효성은 이 문장의 논점 아님
❌ ③ the search engine deleted it: 삭제와 무관한 맥락
det.tip: even though it looks like it is(valid) — '유효해 보이더라도' 양보절. 겉모습과 실제의 괴리

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: but based on the popularity of the content
not based on the accuracy of the information
and based on the relevance of each result
so based on the quality of the sources

det.korean: 정보의 정확성에 근거하지 않고(not based on the accuracy of the information).
det.analysis:
✅ ② not based on the accuracy of the information: 원문 일치. 클릭 기반이지 정확성 기반이 아니라는 대조
❌ ① popularity(인기): 그럴듯하지만 원문은 accuracy
❌ ③ relevance(관련성): 관련성에 기반한다면 오도하지 않음. 핵심 논지와 모순
❌ ④ quality(품질): 원문과 불일치
det.tip: not based on A, but based on B 구조. 검색 엔진은 정확성이 아니라 클릭 패턴에 기반해 학습
